<thought>Based on the mass spectrum, the molecular ion appears at m/z 194.09 with a prominent M+2 peak (~33 % of the base), indicating the presence of a single chlorine atom. The M+1 intensity (~13 %) suggests roughly 12 carbon atoms. A plausible molecular formula is C₁₁H₁₁ClO (exact monoisotopic mass 194.0499 Da), which fits the observed mass and isotopic pattern. This formula has a double‑bond equivalent of 6, consistent with an aromatic ring plus additional unsaturation. The most likely structure is a chlorinated aromatic ketone such as 4‑chlorophenyl‑acetone (SMILES: **CC(=O)Cc1ccc(Cl)cc1**). This SMILES matches the formula C₁₁H₁₁ClO and the expected spectral features. 

<final_answer>CC(=O)Cc1ccc(Cl)cc1</final_answer>
